title: AI Automation
menuDescription: Programming and workflow automation that connects software, data, and repeatable operations.
summary: Practical AI-assisted programming and workflow automation for connected software and repeatable business operations.

overview.title: Automate the work that needs judgment, structure, and reliable handoffs.
paragraphs: We design AI-assisted workflows around a specific operational task, the data it needs, the tools it can use, and the decisions that still require a person.
The goal is not an isolated chatbot. It is a controlled software workflow with clear inputs, outputs, review points, and recovery paths.

features.title: Workflow discovery
features.description: Map the current process, repeated decisions, data sources, exceptions, and human ownership.

features.title: Tool and API actions
features.description: Connect models to approved systems so workflows can retrieve data and perform defined actions.

features.title: Knowledge retrieval
features.description: Ground responses in controlled documents, product data, or vector search when the use case requires it.

features.title: Structured outputs
features.description: Return predictable fields and machine-readable results that downstream software can validate.

features.title: Human review points
features.description: Keep approval, correction, and escalation visible where automated decisions carry business risk.

features.title: Evaluation and monitoring
features.description: Track workflow quality, failures, latency, cost, and the cases that need further tuning.

banner.title: Have a workflow that is repetitive but not fully predictable?
banner.description: Bring us the steps, systems, decisions, and failure cases. We will identify where AI can help safely.

faqs.question: What is a good first AI automation project?
faqs.answer: A focused workflow with clear inputs, repeated effort, measurable output, and a person who owns the result is usually a better start than a broad company-wide assistant.

faqs.question: Which AI providers can you integrate?
faqs.answer: We work with OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, and Google Gemini, and select the provider around the task, data constraints, latency, cost, and integration environment.

faqs.question: Does automation remove people from the workflow?
faqs.answer: Not by default. We identify where people need to approve, correct, or handle exceptions, then make those review points explicit in the software.

faqs.question: Can the workflow use our internal documents and data?
faqs.answer: Yes, when access and governance allow it. Retrieval and permission boundaries are designed around the sources the workflow is approved to use.

faqs.question: How do you handle incorrect AI output?
faqs.answer: We constrain outputs, validate structure, ground responses where appropriate, define confidence and escalation rules, and monitor failure cases instead of treating model output as automatically correct.
